notes: TI gives no multi-band network: its two reference designs are band-specific (315/433 on one PCB with different values, 868/915 on another). Differential load to present: 116+j41 ohm at 315/433, 86.5+j43 ohm at 868/915 (p16).

Open multi-band reference found: Kiisu V4b (github.com/kiisu-io/kiisu4, CERN-OHL-S-2.0, PDF schematics only). It has the Flipper-style two-SP3T bank drawn but unpopulated and feeds the antenna from a wide-band 1:1 balun with 100 pF DC blocks. No harmonic filtering in that build: transmit harmonics are not addressed by the source.
CERN-OHL-S is strongly reciprocal: copying that schematic sheet obliges the same licence on the derived design files. Check against the project's licence decision.

Flipper Zero schematics are published 'for educational purposes only' (docs.flipper.net/zero/development/hardware/schematic) -- not an open licence -- and the sub-GHz PDF could not be downloaded (links are expired signed URLs). Flipper firmware (GPL-3.0) confirms three paths: 299.999755-348.000335, 386.999938-464, 778.999847-928 MHz, selected by one MCU pin plus CC1101 GDO2 (IOCFG2 = HW low, optionally inverted): 433 -> sw0=0, GDO2 high; 315 -> sw0=1, GDO2 low; 868 -> sw0=1, GDO2 high; isolate -> sw0=0, GDO2 low.
27 MHz crystal is recommended by TI above 869 MHz for EN 300 220 bandwidth compliance (p23); 26 MHz is what the brief asks for.
External clock instead of a crystal is allowed on XOSC_Q1 (full-swing 0-VDD digital, or sine <= 1 Vpp through a series capacitor), XOSC_Q2 open (p23-24).
pin_plan_conflicts: CC1101_GDO0 sits on a 1.8 V pad (EMC_B2_19) 'through a divider'. A divider works for receive only. In asynchronous transmit GDO0 is the data INPUT and needs >= VDD-0.7 = 2.6 V with the chip on 3.3 V: a 1.8 V pad cannot drive it. Needs a direction-controlled translator (SN74LVC1T45) or a 3.3 V pad, or split: RX data out on GDO2 (divider) and TX data in on GDO0 (1.8->3.3 V buffer).
No pin is planned for GDO2 and none for the band-switch / antenna-switch controls: 2-4 expander lines needed.
